customer.primary_segment: Solo commercial brokers and small brokerage teams without in-house marketing/design staff, doing roughly 5-20 deals/year [0,1,2,4]
customer.secondary_segment: New/independent agents and small syndicators priced out of enterprise CRE marketing software (Buildout $125-500+/user/mo) [1,4]
customer.pain_point: OM production is time-consuming (~2 work weeks/yr at 20 deals) and brokers actively ask peers what tool to use [0,3]

offer.page_count_range: 15-72 pages/slides depending on tier; ~20-49 pages is the common mid-market band [5,7,8,9]
offer.core_sections: Cover/TOC, executive summary, property overview, photos/maps, demographics/market, rent roll & pro forma financials, tenant/comparables, contact/CTA [6,10]
offer.formats: Editable Canva (Etsy low/mid tier), PowerPoint (vip.graphics, offeringmemos.com), Adobe InDesign or PowerPoint (BTS Brands agency tier) [5,6,7]
offer.bonuses: Fill-in guides on Etsy listings; 1-click font/color rebranding themes on the PPT tier; done-for-you retainer add-on at the agency tier [6,21]

acquisition.channels: Etsy organic search + paid Etsy Ads on exact-match terms; Pinterest idea/board pages; shop-linked Instagram [11,12,13]
acquisition.search_terms: 'offering memorandum template', 'commercial offering memorandum', 'CIM template', 'commercial real estate offering memorandum'
acquisition.niche_size_signal: Review counts (18-91) on CRE-OM listings are an order of magnitude lower than generic real-estate-template listings (1k-2k+ reviews), implying a small but real underserved niche [15]
acquisition.marketplace_gap: Creative Market and Canva's own marketplace show little/no CRE-OM-specific inventory, leaving Etsy plus a few standalone shops (vip.graphics, BTS Brands, offeringmemos.com) as the main venues [16]

sales.price_ladder: $10-20 DIY Canva (existing claims) -> $17.99-$79.99 Etsy mid-tier -> $99/$249 PowerPoint license tiers -> $295 agency-built [17,18,19,20,22,23]
sales.ladder_logic: Price scales with page count, format flexibility (Canva vs PPT/InDesign), and license breadth (1 project vs unlimited vs done-for-you) [23]
sales.license_model: Higher tiers sell reuse rights (unlimited own projects) rather than resale rights; resale is contractually excluded at every tier observed [20,27]

fulfillment.build_effort: Must design 15-70+ pages/slides across ~8-10 recurring OM sections; property photography is explicitly excluded/placeholder at the premium agency tier and must be sourced separately [8,24]
fulfillment.licensing_constraints: Canva Pro/stock elements cannot be resold standalone or with only minimal modification; templates must add substantial original design work, and are typically distributed as duplicable template links rather than raw asset files [25,26]
fulfillment.resale_constraint: Even paid premium templates (vip.graphics) explicitly forbid resale/distribution by the buyer, confirming template creators must build original layouts rather than relicense a purchased template [27]

economics.estimate_basis: Etsy review count x assumed ~8-10 sales-per-review ratio (assumption, not disclosed by Etsy) [29,30]
economics.multi_channel_leverage: One built asset (vip.graphics PPT) is resold across 2+ storefronts at 3 price points, suggesting a single well-built template can be repackaged for more revenue than one listing alone [31]
economics.caveat: All figures here are estimates with an explicit, unverifiable assumption about review-to-sale ratio [32]

history.generic_entry_pattern: Template Etsy sellers typically launch a single low-priced ($10-20) listing first and expand only after initial sales validate demand, per a generic (non-CRE) seller case study [33]
history.niche_focused_competitor: At least one real CRE-specific competitor (StructuredCreativeCo) appears to have stayed narrowly focused on real-estate templates rather than diversifying [34]
history.agency_precedent: Full-service OM design agencies (BTS Brands) have served brokerages since 2013, i.e. the $295+ done-for-you tier predates today's $10-80 self-serve Etsy/Canva tier [35]

smallest_viable_version: A single Etsy listing: one 15-20 page editable Canva template (distributed as a shareable Canva template link, not a resold file, to respect Canva's licensing terms) covering the 6 core OM sections -- cover, executive summary, property overview, financials/rent roll, demographics/map, contact/CTA -- priced around $15-25 to match the lowest-friction competitor tier, with the owner's own commercial-broker contact list (60 brokers, 56 CRE CPAs) used for initial direct outreach/testimonials rather than paid ads. Photos and market data are the buyer's responsibility (own listing photos), keeping the seller's fulfillment burden to design-and-list only, matching how the cheapest real competitors already operate.
disagreements: vip.graphics' own site prices the 44+ slide PPT template at $99 (commercial)/$249 (extended), while its own referral funnel offeringmemos.com sells what appears to be the same core template for $36 -- a 2.75x-6.9x price spread for the same asset across channels.

IntellCRE's content (a competing SaaS vendor) argues templates only 'solve the design problem, not the content problem' and are inadequate for serious brokers -- this is vendor content marketing for a competing paid tool and should be weighted as biased, not neutral, evidence about template demand.
